text:
Washington arrives in Nashville on the second night of a back-to-back, a night after beating Philadelphia 5-2, and they are playing without Vincent Desharnais. The Capitals are 4-1-0 in their last five. The Predators are 2-1-2 and still sorting out a 4-3 shootout loss to the Islanders, a game in which Brayden Schenn reached 300 career goals. Washington also lands in the middle of a five-game Nashville home stand, game three.

The Capitals have controlled more of the play at five on five, taking 53% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) to Nashville's 45%. Our model has the game almost even: 3.27 expected goals for Washington, 3.20 for Nashville. Washington takes 4.5 penalties a night, which feeds a Predators power play that produces 0.66 expected goals a game. In net, projected starter Charlie Lindgren is at -0.5 goals saved above expected this season (how many goals a goalie stops beyond what the shots should allow), while projected Juuse Saros is at +3.8, though Saros was at -10.2 over 59 games last year and Lindgren at -5.9 over 21.

Alex Tuch is our top Washington scorer at 41%, and as Tom Gulitti of NHL.com posted, he is "up to 8 goals in 11 games this season." Jordan Kyrou plays his 500th game on a five-game point streak. For Nashville, Steven Stamkos is 38% to score and Ryan O'Reilly 36%. Our under-the-radar picks are Adam Edstrom, who shoots from dangerous spots on the third line (20% to score), and Alexander Kerfoot, at 41% for a point against a Capitals defense that gives up the fifth-most expected goals per 60.
